## My thinking, season by season

I've been working this land for 50 years now. My wife and I manage 9 mu between us — six mu on the wheat-maize rotation, three mu in cotton out on the western plot where the soil is a bit lighter. The children are in the city; it's just the two of us, so I have to think carefully about labor. I went through senior high back in the seventies, and I read the extension bulletins when they come around, so I plan my rates rather than just guessing.

### Wheat (6 mu)

I'll drill my wheat around October 10-15, after I've cleared the maize stover. I use an improved semi-dwarf variety — Jimai-type, about 35 yuan/mu for seed. Based on last year's 460 kg/mu and the residual N from the maize stover I incorporated, I'm targeting 480 kg/mu this year. That means about 18 kg N/mu total — I put 10 kg down as compound fertilizer at sowing (18-18-18 or similar), then topdress 8 kg of urea at jointing in March if the crop looks pale. Phosphorus and potash I handle through the compound at base. I'll irrigate four times: winter water in December, then jointing, heading, and grain-fill. Each irrigation costs me roughly 30 yuan/mu in electricity at the well. I'll spray herbicide once for broadleaves in spring and keep an eye out for powdery mildew and scab at heading — if the weather turns humid I'll spray tebuconazole.

### Maize (6 mu, same fields)

Very tight turnaround after wheat — I combine-harvest the wheat around June 10, and I want maize in the ground by June 15. I use a no-till planter hired from the village service, about 40 yuan/mu. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Denghai, roughly 50 yuan/mu. I apply 15 kg N/mu — about 6 kg at planting as compound, then side-dress 9 kg urea at the V8-V10 stage. Usually I only need one irrigation at tasseling if the July rains come as expected; in a dry year I'll give it a second at grain-fill. Herbicide at planting, one shot of insecticide if I see corn borer. Target yield is 520 kg/mu.

### Cotton (3 mu)

Cotton is where I'm slowing down. The picking is hard on my back and my wife's, and labor's expensive if I hire. I'm keeping the three mu for now because the western plot isn't well-suited to maize and I have the experience. I'll transplant seedlings in late April after the soil warms, Bt variety — that saves me on bollworm sprays, which is why I stick with it. About 14 kg N/mu, split across base and two topdresses at squaring and flowering. Two irrigations — one before flowering, one at peak bolling. I'll pinch tops in late July to control growth. Yield expectation 250 kg/mu lint. I'll hire two days of picking help in October; my wife and I can't get through three mu alone anymore.

### Budget and tradeoffs

Total input spend comes to around 6,500 yuan across the 9 mu. The biggest line is fertilizer, then irrigation electricity, then cotton picking labor. I could cut the fourth wheat irrigation if May is wet, and I will — no sense pumping water the sky is giving me free. What I won't cut is the jointing topdress on wheat; I tried that one year in the nineties and lost nearly 80 kg/mu. That lesson stuck.
